speaker: Doctor
text: That is an unusual start to our conversation; to help me understand your sudden abdominal pain, could you please tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it has radiated to any other area?

speaker: Patient
text: 74-year-old male. The patient presents with sudden onset of abdominal pain around the umbilicus 16 hours ago, with recent history of hospitalization for an acute myocardial infarction a week ago. Reports several episodes of bloody loose bowel movements. Denies vomiting.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Mesenteric Ischemia. The combination of recent myocardial infarction, sudden onset periumbilical pain, and bloody stools in a 74-year-old male is highly suggestive of acute mesenteric ischemia, likely due to embolization. I need to confirm this with imaging immediately. REQUEST TEST: CT Angiography of the Abdomen and Pelvis. REQUEST IMAGES.
